title: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
subtitle: Mycosis fungoides · Sézary syndrome · primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs — a chronic disease managed for years: skin-directed first, systemic by compartment (skin vs blood), transplant for the few who can be cured
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Mycosis Fungoides/Sézary Syndrome (Chou L, Khodadoust M) · NCCN Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: What you are dealing with
rows: Most common CTCL. Patch → plaque → tumor, often in sun-protected “bathing-trunk” skin. Epidermotropic CD4+ cells, CD7 loss, Pautrier microabscesses. Skin-resident memory T-cell origin
All three: erythroderma (≥80% BSA) + B2 blood + a blood clone matching the skin. Central-memory origin — a leukemic disease, not simply late MF
Folliculotropic (independent predictor of progression and death) · large-cell transformation (>25% large cells; higher progression risk) · tumor stage, raised LDH
Primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs 2nd most common CTCL

Lymphomatoid papulosis and primary cutaneous ALCL — indolent, excellent prognosis despite anaplastic cytology. Distinguish from systemic ALCL spreading to skin (ALK+ = systemic until proven otherwise)
blocks.footnote: A TCR clone alone is not diagnostic — clonal T cells occur in benign dermatoses. Early MF often needs several biopsies, ideally taken off topical steroids.

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Skin biopsy (multiple sites) with IHC incl. CD30 and TCR gene rearrangement; measure BSA (patient palm + fingers ≈ 1%) and mSWAT
Blood flow cytometry (CD4:CD8, CD4+CD7−, CD4+CD26− absolute counts) + blood TCR clone — needed to assign B stage
Imaging: PET/CT or CT for T2b and above, palpable nodes, or B1–B2 blood. Stage IA with no nodes needs no imaging
Excise an abnormal node — nodal histology (N1–N3) changes the stage; marrow only if unexplained cytopenias
LDH, CBC, CMP; HTLV-1 serology if erythroderma or from an endemic area (ATLL mimics Sézary)

blocks.heading: ISCL/EORTC TNMB (Olsen, Blood 2022)
rows: Patches/plaques <10% · ≥10% BSA (a = patch only, b = plaque)
Abnormal node, histology Dutch grade 1 / 2 / 3–4 (NCI LN 0–2 / 3 / 4)
≤5% Sézary cells, or <250/µL, or <15% CD4+CD26− / CD4+CD7−
More than B0 but not B2
≥1,000/µL Sézary cells, or CD4+CD26− / CD4+CD7− / other aberrant cells by flow — plus a blood clone matching the skin

blocks.heading: Stage groups
blocks.footnote: Stage IA: 5-yr OS 94%, median survival ≥20 yr — most die of something else. Stage III–IV: median survival ~5 yr, and over half die of disease (Agar, JCO 2010; NCI PDQ).

boxes: not curative — do not escalate for cosmetics
add a low-intensity systemic: bexarotene, IFN,
limited tumors: local RT 8–12 Gy + skin therapy
ECP ± IFN or bexarotene — lower blood burden
TSEBT often used to debulk skin pre-transplant

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — skin-directed and systemic therapy, supportive care, CD30+ LPDs and trials

blocks.heading: Skin-directed therapy
rows: High-potency (clobetasol) BID for T1 patches — high response rates in limited disease. Atrophy, striae, HPA suppression with large BSA
Daily thin layer to lesions; gel non-inferior to compounded ointment (CAILS ORR 59% vs 48%), faster response. Contact dermatitis ~20% — reduce frequency, add topical steroid. No systemic absorption
Retinoid gel titrated to BID–QID for limited lesions; irritation. Imiquimod for thick single plaques
nbUVB for patches, PUVA for thicker plaques (deeper penetration); 2–3×/wk to clearance, then taper. Cumulative risk of skin cancer (PUVA: SCC, melanoma); eye protection after psoralen
8–12 Gy per lesion for palliation; 24–30 Gy for unilesional disease (curative intent). MF is exquisitely radiosensitive
12 Gy low-dose (1 Gy ×12): ORR 88%, CR 27%, median clinical benefit ~71 wk, repeatable. 30–36 Gy gives deeper CR but more toxicity and only once or twice per lifetime
blocks.footnote: Maximise skin-directed therapy and supportive care first — it lengthens time to the next systemic. Check that a systemic agent is compatible with phototherapy/TSEBT before combining.

blocks.heading: Primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs — do not over-treat
items: Lymphomatoid papulosis: crops of papules that self-heal in weeks. No therapy changes survival — observe, topical steroids, phototherapy, or low-dose weekly MTX for scarring or frequent crops. Lifelong follow-up: associated second lymphomas (MF, ALCL, Hodgkin)
Primary cutaneous ALCL: solitary/localized nodules, >75% CD30+, ALK−. Excision or RT; multifocal → MTX or brentuximab. Staging CT/PET to exclude systemic ALCL

blocks.heading: Systemic therapy — dosing, evidence, monitoring
rows: 300 mg/m²/day with food; often started lower and titrated

ORR 45% in refractory IIB–IVB. Hypertriglyceridemia (pancreatitis) — start fenofibrate first, avoid gemfibrozil (raises bexarotene levels). Central hypothyroidism: TSH falls — dose levothyroxine to free T4. Teratogen
3–6 MU SC daily or TIW (pegylated IFN now used — Intron A off market)
Flu-like symptoms, depression, cytopenias, thyroid. Pairs well with ECP, bexarotene, PUVA
Workhorse for MF and LyP. LFTs, CBC; switch to pralatrexate 15 mg/m² if more is needed
ORR 30%, pruritus relief 32%. Diarrhea, fatigue, thrombocytopenia, PE 5%
ORR 34%, DOR 15 mo, pruritus better in 43%. Nausea; QTc — replete K/Mg. CTCL approval intact
ALCANZA (CD30 ≥10%): ORR4 56% vs 13%, PFS 16.7 vs 3.5 mo. Neuropathy 67%. Best for plaques/tumors, LCT, pc-ALCL
1 mg/kg IV d1, 8, 15, 22 of cycle 1, then d1, 15 q28d

MAVORIC: PFS 7.7 vs 3.1 mo; ORR 28% vs 5%, Sézary 37% vs 2% — blood clears best. Drug eruption in ~24%, median onset 119 days, mimics progression — biopsy + clonality before calling relapse. Deplete Tregs: raises GVHD if given shortly before allo-HCT
9 µg/kg/day IV d1–5 q21d, up to 8 cycles
FDA Aug 2024, stage I–III after ≥1 systemic: ORR 36%, CR 9%. Capillary leak 20% (boxed) — weight, albumin, edema; infusion reactions, hepatotoxicity
Erythrodermic / Sézary with modest blood burden; nearly non-immunosuppressive. Combine with IFN or bexarotene
ORR 38% in advanced MF/SS; Sézary flare (erythroderma, itch) in 53% — not progression
3 mg d1, then 10 mg SC TIW, max 12 wk
Sézary / blood only (skips skin-resident MF cells). CMV PCR q2–3 wk + acyclovir + TMP-SMX. Off the US market — access program
Gem 1,000 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d · PLD 10–30 mg/m² q2–4wk · pralatrexate 15 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d
For tumor stage and LCT. Pralatrexate at half the PTCL dose, with B12/folate
blocks.footnote: Lacutamab (anti-KIR3DL2) has breakthrough designation for Sézary but is not approved; phase 3 TELLOMAK-3 starting 2026. Multi-agent chemotherapy (CHOP, ICE, GDP) gives short responses and heavy infection risk — reserve for bridging.

blocks.heading: Itch, skin barrier and infection
items: S. aureus colonizes ~50% of erythrodermic patients and drives flares: in one series, eradication (oral antibiotics + intranasal mupirocin) cleared carriage in >85% and improved the skin in 58%. MRSA is common — TMP-SMX or doxycycline empirically
Dilute bleach baths, emollients, wet wraps; culture before calling progression — infection and drug eruption both mimic it
Bacteremia from skin portals is a major risk in erythrodermic disease — avoid lines through involved skin when possible
Pruritus: often the dominant symptom; antihistamines rarely enough. Gabapentin, mirtazapine, aprepitant; disease control is the best antipruritic (romidepsin 43%, vorinostat 32% itch relief)
Lifelong skin-cancer surveillance after PUVA, TSEBT and mechlorethamine

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Mogamulizumab vs vorinostat — PFS 7.7 vs 3.1 mo, HR 0.53; Sézary ORR 37% vs 2%
BV vs MTX/bexarotene, CD30+ MF or pc-ALCL — ORR4 56% vs 13%
Allo-HCT vs none (donor availability) — PFS 9.0 vs 3.0 mo, HR 0.38
Mechlorethamine gel vs ointment — non-inferior, faster
